To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microRNA miR124 promotes neuronal differentiation, in part, by triggering brain specific pre-mRNA alternative splicing.

the neuron specific miRNA miR 128 promotes neuronal differentiation by targeting the PTBP1 mRNA and thereby increasing the levels of the NS specific PTBP2 protein, which in turn triggers a switch from non NS to neuronal alternative splicing.
the microRNA miR124 regulates alternative pre mRNA spicing in the nervous system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of microRNAs in neuronal differentiation and brain development.
the role of microRNAs in the differentiation of the nervous system.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of the mammalian nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microRNA miR124 promotes neuronal differentiation through a mechanism that involves the regulation of pre mRNA alternative splicing and the PTB/PTBP family of proteins.

miR 24 is a key regulator of neuronal differentiation, which promotes neuronal differentiation by targeting PTB, a global repressor, and thereby allowing for the accumulation of nPTB, an activator of alternative splicing.
miR 24 promotes NS development, by regulating an intricate alternative splicing network, which is controlled by PTB and nPTB.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
miR 24 promotes neuronal differentiation by regulating the alternative splicing of a number of genes.
miR 128 promotes neuronal differentiation by targeting the splicing regulator PTBP1, thereby allowing PTBP2, another splicing regulator, to accumulate and trigger NS specific alternative splicings.
the microRNA miR124 promotes neuronal differentiation through a mechanism that involves direct regulation of PTBP1 and alternative pre mRNA processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microRNA miR124 promotes neuronal differentiation through the regulation of a global splicing regulator, PTBP1, and that miR124 is required for neuronal differentiation.
